keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no French West Africa row). Page: 'Originally created in 1895 as a union of Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast only'. Modern country outlines stand in for the four colonies' claims; the Mossi country (Burkina Faso) is held back until its 1901 conquest, though it lay inside the French Sudan and Ivory Coast claims. Infobox area 4,689,000 km2 (no year given) is the whole late federation; the gazetteer resolves these four modern countries to about 2.33 M km2 (cell count), about half the infobox figure, as expected before the Mossi country, Dahomey, Mauritania and Niger joined.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Dahomey was added in 1904'; 'In 1904, both Mauritania and Niger were classed Military Territories' (federation page) and 'Mauritania thus became part of French West Africa in 1904' (History of Mauritania, which this keyframe follows; the federation page also says 'Mauritania was added in 1920'). Niger is held back to 1922.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Niger 'became a French colony in 1922' (History of Niger); the federation page lists Niger among the eight constituents but also says it stayed out 'until the 1920s and 1940s respectively'. The gazetteer resolves the eight modern countries to about 4.97 M km2 (cell count), ratio 1.06 to the infobox 4,689,000 km2 (no year given), so the outline is sound. Upper Volta was dismembered in 1932 and restored on 4 September 1947 without changing the federation's outline; Guinea leaves in 1958.

region.text: Samory's lands in southern Guinea, northern Ivory Coast and the Wassoulou of Sikasso; the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 1895: the French are still fighting Samory Ture's Wassoulou empire (campaigns of 1891 and 1893 on the Wassoulou page; 'In March 10, 1891, a French force under Colonel Louis Archinard set out from Nyamina for a surprise attack on Kankan'; early 1893 Faranah is taken). The page is silent on 1894-1897, so the start at the federation's founding is a bridging judgment.

region.text: Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast: 'Originally created in 1895 as a union of Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast only'

ledger.note: 1895 (27 October): French West Africa is created at Saint-Louis as a union of Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast. Infobox 'Established: 27 October 1895'; 'Originally created in 1895 as a union of Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast only'. The French Sudan already included the Toucouleur lands: 'In 1893 the French took final control, ending the empire' (Toucouleur Empire page), and 'They captured Nioro in 1891' (same page).
1896: the French claim the Mossi country. 'The French arrived and claimed the area in 1896, but Mossi resistance ended only with the capture of their capital' Ouagadougou in 1901.

region.text: the lands of Samoridugu, the Wassoulou empire (page names no territory)

ledger.note: 1898 (29 September): Samory is captured and his empire ends. 'the French captain Henri Gouraud surprised Toure's forces at Guelemou on September 29, 1898'; 'With his capture, Samoridugu ceased to exist.' The page does not say which lands France then held, so the region is the Wassoulou of the gazetteer plus the Guinea-Ivory Coast hinterland.
1898 (29 September): fighting with Samory ends with his capture at Guelemou by Captain Gouraud.
1901: Ouagadougou falls and the Mossi country is French. 'Mossi resistance ended only with the capture of their capital' Ouagadougou 'in 1901'.
1901: the Mossi resistance ends with the capture of Ouagadougou.
1902: the governor-general moves from Saint-Louis to Dakar. 'A governor-general was based first in Saint-Louis, then (from 1902) in Dakar'; infobox 'Saint-Louis (1895-1902), then Dakar'.

1904: Dahomey joins the federation. 'Dahomey was added in 1904, after having been put under colonial tutelage in 1892.' The kingdom of Dahomey itself fell to France in 1894 (French Africa dossier). Counterpart set to french-africa by the reviewer (af-08-x review, 2026-10-24): the Kingdom of Dahomey dossier ends in January 1894, and the colony of Dahomey that joined the federation in 1904 was French land.

1904: Mauritania becomes part of French West Africa. 'Mauritania thus became part of French West Africa in 1904' (History of Mauritania); the federation page has it a Military Territory in 1904 and 'added' in 1920, so 1904 and 1920 are two readings of one process. The page names no previous state; the Moorish emirates (Trarza, Brakna) have dossiers from af-03-x but are not named on the pages opened.

1922: Niger becomes a French colony within the West African system. 'Niger became a French colony in 1922' and 'dissident ethnic groups, especially the desert Tuareg, were not subdued until 1922'; the federation page puts Niger among the eight constituents but says elsewhere it stayed outside 'until the 1920s and 1940s'. fx-27: counterpart changed from nobody to french-africa. Cliopatria's French Africa row, which the french-africa dossier carries, already held Niger (4,456 cells from the 1900s to 1921), so a gain from nobody took no cell and the 1922 keyframe then had to add all of Niger in one jump. History of Niger: "French colonial rule began in the late 19th century, with Niger becoming a French colony in 1922"; "French efforts at pacification began before 1900" and the Tuareg "were not subdued until 1922".

region.text: French Togoland, a League of Nations mandate administered with Dahomey

ledger.note: 1934: the League of Nations mandate of French Togoland is attached to Dahomey. 'Between 1934 and 1937, the League of Nations Mandate territory of French Togoland was subsumed into Dahomey.'
1937: the Togoland attachment to Dahomey ends (the page gives the span 1934-1937).
1958: Guinea votes for independence. 'All colonies except Guinea voted to remain'; Guinea 'voted overwhelmingly for independence' in the referendum on the Fifth Republic's constitution.

region.text: the seven territories that stayed in the French Community

ledger.note: 1958: the federation ceases to exist. 'Legally, the federation ceased to exist after the 1958 French constitutional referendum'; infobox 'Fifth Republic: 5 October 1958'; the lead says the federation 'existed from 1895 until 1958'. Its territories remain autonomous republics of the French Community until 1960, when Senegal and Sudan form the Mali Federation (20 June 1960, split 20 August 1960) and the rest become independent.

wars.name: French conquest of the Wassoulou Empire

zones.text: Samory's lands in Guinea, Ivory Coast and the Wassoulou

wars.outcome: French victory: Samory captured by Gouraud at Guelemou on 29 September 1898 and 'Samoridugu ceased to exist'.
wars.note: The page gives the treaties of 1886 (Kenieba Koura: the Niger as the border), Bissandougou (1887) and Niako (February 1889), the French attack on Kankan (10 March 1891) and Faranah (early 1893). The war article itself was not opened.

wars.name: French conquest of the Mossi country
wars.note: The page gives no campaign detail beyond 1896 (French arrival) and 1901 (capture of Ouagadougou).

certainty.note: Inland and Saharan frontiers (Mauritania, Niger, French Sudan north) are administrative and approximate; frontiers against Gambia, the Gold Coast and Nigeria were fixed by treaties that no page opened gives. Colony-level boundaries were redrawn by decree (Upper Volta 1919 or 1921, dismembered 1932, restored 4 September 1947).

notes:
French West Africa is a colony-type federation inside Cliopatria's French Africa row (1846-1957), which draws every French territory in Africa as one shape; this dossier gives the federation its own outline and dates. Cliopatria has no row for it, so every keyframe is new and built from modern country outlines, which overstate the 1895-1900 French position inland.
Disagreements between pages: Mauritania joins in 1904 (History of Mauritania) or 1920 (federation page); Upper Volta is made in 1919 from Ivory Coast provinces (History of Burkina Faso) or in 1921 by splitting French Sudan (federation page); Niger is a constituent in the infobox but 'out of the federation until the 1940s' in the text. The dossier follows the country pages for the dates and lists the other reading in each note.
Pages that were thin: the federation article has no section on the conquest and gives no Governors-General; the three 'History of' pages and the Wassoulou and Toucouleur pages give years but not boundaries. The 1895-1900 shape therefore does not show the unfinished conquest of the hinterland; the contest zones for Samory (1895-98) and the Mossi (1896-1901) mark it. The Franco-Dahomean wars and Archinard's Soudan campaigns (Nioro 1891, the Toucouleur empire ended 1893) precede the founding and are carried by the French Africa dossier.
Not covered for want of a page in the budget: the Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea conquest details, the 1932 Upper Volta partition by colony, the 1947 restoration as an outline change (internal), the Kaocen and Tuareg wars in Niger, the 1912 Adrar conquest, Vichy-era loyalties (1940-42, Dakar), and the exact autonomy dates of 1958-60. Counterparts needing dossiers: french-togoland (1916-1957, League of Nations mandate). The Mali Federation (1959-60) has its own dossier (mali-federation).
Gazetteer: no new names needed (Sikasso admin1 carries 'Wassoulou' as an alias).
